module_mood_contract: M0 prework — not on the mood arc (mood arc opens at M1: joyful creation). Prework is almost entirely SETUP/LAUNCH beat (repo pick, session open, tarball fetch, extract+install, arrival hand-off, optional pre-read), mood-exempt per check_strategy_tie_in §1. Step 5 (pick a trivial bug + confirm readiness) is the sole TEACHING beat — rehearses the push-back move that recurs across the training. Close hands off verbatim into M1's Connections question, priming joyful creation without pre-empting it.

personas.name: opinionated_senior
confusions: Mild resistance in 'What to bring' to being walked through backlog sizing already known — temperament, not a comprehension gap; resolves on its own.

personas.name: fast_operator
confusions: Skimming 'What to bring' risks reading the four task sizes as stages of one task rather than four separate backlog items — the correcting bolded line sits in prose this reader is likely to skip. Self-correcting downstream, not silent, but not caught here.

Step 5's push-back rehearsal is contingent on BOTH the body sentence being read AND Claude actually dumping all four criteria in one message; a body-skipping reader whose run screens cleanly never exercises the recovery move and has no way of knowing they missed it. The visible end-state artifact is identical to the other two personas' — only the trace shows the practice was thinner.

triangle_disagreement: The three personas do NOT converge on step 5 (the file's sole teaching beat). The mid-layer-competent read scores it 8/10 — the rehearsal fires cleanly and lands as intended. The opinionated-senior read scores it 7/10 for a DIFFERENT reason: the beat still narrates a push-back move this persona already owns by instinct, so it reads as slightly over-explained rather than under-delivered — the fix is dosage (name the recovery prompt as available, not prescribed), not mechanism. The fast-operator read also scores 7/10, but for a THIRD, more structural reason: the forcing function's trigger is a conjunction of (a) the reader actually reading the body sentence naming the failure mode, and (b) Claude actually dumping all four criteria in one message on that run — neither is forced by the prompt itself, so a fast, prompt-only reader whose run screens cleanly skips the rehearsal entirely without any signal that anything was missed. Reported separately per the run's instruction rather than averaged into one 7.3: the senior's 7 is a dosage complaint (harmless, arguably correct as designed), the fast operator's 7 is a coverage gap in the forcing function's trigger condition (worth a fix_hint, not a REVISE, since no persona actually fell below the mood floor and the visible arrival artifact is complete for all three).

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Forcing functions live in prompts, not body prose.
rules_evaluated.evidence: The step-5 push-back move is enacted by the registry prompt `{{prompt:ae101-prework-one-at-a-time}}`, and the mid-layer and opinionated-senior persona reads both fire it as designed (persona.json personas[0].phases[6], personas[1].phases[6]). The fast-operator triangle leg surfaces a real edge rule §16 itself names as the risk to check ('Speed-runners skip body'): the recovery cue lives in body prose ahead of the fenced screening prompt, and the fast-operator read (persona.json personas[2].phases[6]) skips that sentence and, on a run where Claude screens cleanly, never exercises the rehearsal at all — not because the reader missed a fence, but because the trigger condition (body-read AND Claude-misstep) isn't forced by the prompt. Harm check: is this the harm §16 exists to prevent (a load-bearing forcing function silently unavailable to a real reading style)? Partially — the artifact this persona leaves prework with (bug picked, readiness confirmed) is unaffected, so nothing downstream breaks; only the SKILL rehearsal is thinner for this one persona on this one run, and only probabilistically (contingent on Claude's own behavior that turn, not deterministic). That's a coverage gap worth a fix_hint, not a structural §16 violation — the fence still carries a real forcing function ('one at a time'), it's just reactive rather than always-fired. Not blocking.
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Consider folding a self-report into the primary screening prompt (e.g. ask Claude to name whether it paced the three candidates or presented them together) so the tell surfaces even on a clean run and even for a reader who skipped the body sentence — makes the rehearsal fire regardless of reading style, not just regardless of Claude's phrasing.

'Come to Module 1 without one and you'll be scrambling for one while the exercise is already fixing bugs. Your call.' (Bring to Module 1) — names the consequence, not a wrongdoing; 'Your call' keeps the frame descriptive rather than shaming. All three persona mood_notes at this phase (persona.json phases[7]) read it as epistemic; the opinionated-senior record explicitly notes the 'your call' framing as respecting a persona that dislikes being told what to do.
